items.problem: The migration agent trusted a green 10s smoke launch and shipped a blank app. The blank page was caused by a NullReferenceException swallowed by a nested scenario Frame, so the process stayed alive.
items.evidence: session-log.txt lines 1926-1930/1957-1958 ('app stayed alive 10s', PASS); score notes UIA tree = 'Navigation to Scenario1_Orientation failed: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.'
items.skill_search: grep 'stayed alive', 'Validator catches this race', 'smoke launch' in SKILL.md / MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md
items.wrong_text_if_any: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md ~line 291: 'Validator catches this race with a 10s smoke launch after the build healthcheck passes.'
items.root_cause: The claim is only true when the null-static read reaches the ROOT frame and crashes the process. When the offending page is reached through a NESTED content Frame (NavigationView scenario frame), Frame.Navigate marshals the exception into NavigationFailed without terminating the process, so the smoke launch reports green on a blank page. The overconfident claim gave the agent false assurance.
items.proposed_fix: Correct the sentence to say the smoke launch only catches the race when it crashes the root/process; a throw in a nested scenario frame is swallowed (blank page, process alive) and must be caught by a per-scenario render check (cross-link silent-navigation-failures).
items.generalizes: Every NavigationView/Frame-based SDK-sample migration has nested-frame navigation. A null-static init-order read (or any page-load throw) in a scenario page is systematically swallowed, so relying on the process-alive smoke launch under-reports blank pages across scenarios.

items.problem: DisplayInformation static/instance members other than GetForCurrentView() are undetected and undocumented, so the agent left DisplayInformation.AutoRotationPreferences (get/set) in place — a runtime trap in WinUI 3 desktop.
items.evidence: Scenario1_Orientation.xaml.cs line 55 (get) and line 77 (set) use DisplayInformation.AutoRotationPreferences; unsupported-api-inventory.json only matches \bGetForCurrentView\s*\( so no TODO was injected for these lines.
items.skill_search: grep 'DisplayInformation', 'AutoRotation', 'DisplayOrientation' across skill — only DisplayInformation.GetForCurrentView() appears (PATTERNS.md#getforcurrentview); AutoRotationPreferences/CurrentOrientation/NativeOrientation/OrientationChanged absent.
items.root_cause: DisplayInformation is CoreWindow/ApplicationView-bound; its members compile but throw at runtime in desktop. The inventory pattern only catches the GetForCurrentView() form, missing the static AutoRotationPreferences and other members, so no TODO/defer signal is produced.
items.proposed_fix: (Tier 1) Add an 'adaptable' inventory entry matching \bDisplayInformation\b routed to the getforcurrentview anchor so a TODO is injected. (Tier 3) Expand PATTERNS.md#getforcurrentview to document that DisplayInformation static/instance members (AutoRotationPreferences get/set, CurrentOrientation, NativeOrientation, OrientationChanged) are view-bound and throw at runtime: orientation READ -> Win32 EnumDisplaySettings; auto-rotation LOCK -> no desktop equivalent.
items.generalizes: Any display-orientation / screen-rotation / DPI sample uses DisplayInformation beyond GetForCurrentView(). Detecting and documenting the whole type prevents recurring silent runtime traps across those scenarios.
